arguments.command:
python3 -c "
import parse

# Check all the test cases for time formats
test_cases = [
    ('10:21:36 +1000', '+1000'),       # aest
    ('10:21:36 +10:00', '+10:00'),     # aest
    ('10:21:36 +0100', '+0100'),       # tz60
    ('10:21:36 +01:00', '+01:00'),     # tz60
    ('10:21:36 +1:00', '+1:00'),       # Same as above?
    ('10:21:36 PM -530', '-530'),      # t530
    ('10:21:36 PM -5:30', '-5:30'),    # t530
    ('10:21:36 PM -0530', '-0530'),    # t530
    ('10:21:36 PM -05:30', '-05:30'),  # t530
]

for case, expected_name in test_cases:
    r = parse.parse('{:tt}', case)
    if r:
        actual_name = r.fixed[0].tzinfo.tzname(None)
        status = 'OK' if actual_name == expected_name else f'MISMATCH (got {actual_name!r})'
        print(f'{case:25s} -> name={actual_name!r} [{status}]')
    else:
        print(f'{case:25s} -> No match')
"

raw_message.reasoning:
This confirms the issue. When parsing "+0100", the FixedTzOffset stores "+0100" as its name, but when comparing to a FixedTzOffset(60, '+01:00'), they're not equal because the names differ.

Now I understand what Bug 92 might be about - the timezone offset formatting should be normalized so that equivalent offsets are treated consistently. The fix should normalize the tz name to a standard format like "+HHMM" (4 characters) or "+HH:MM" (5 characters).
